Name: Draw distance
Description: The number of tiles to draw in either direction from the camera, up to a maximum of 184. Depending on where the scene is centered, you might only see 16 tiles in one direction, unless you extend map loading.

Name: Detail distance
Description: The number of tiles to draw animated models in either direction from the camera, up to a maximum of 184. Reducing this can help with performance, particularly in crowded sailing areas.

Name: Extended map loading
Description: How much further the map should be loaded. The maximum is 5 extra chunks. Note: extending the map can have a very high impact on performance.

Name: Hide unrelated areas
Description: Hide unrelated areas which you shouldn't see from your current position.

Name: Anti-aliasing
Description: Improves pixelated edges at the cost of significantly higher GPU usage. MSAA x16 is very expensive, so x8 is recommended if anti-aliasing is desired.

Name: Game resolution
Description: Render the game at a different resolution and stretch it to fit the screen. Reducing this can improve performance, particularly on very high-resolution displays.

Name: Game scaling mode
Description: The sampling function to use when upscaling the above reduced game resolution.

Name: UI scaling mode
Description: The sampling function to use when the Stretched Mode plugin is enabled. Affects how the UI looks with non-integer scaling.

Name: Anisotropic filtering
Description: Configures whether mipmapping and anisotropic filtering should be used. At zero, mipmapping is disabled and textures look the most pixelated. At 1 through 16, mipmapping is enabled, and textures look more blurry and smoothed out. The higher you go beyond 1, the less blurry textures will look, to a certain extent.

Name: Normal mapping
Description: Affects how light interacts with certain materials. Barely impacts performance.

Name: Parallax occlusion mapping
Description: Adds more depth to some materials, at the cost of higher GPU usage.

Name: Unlock FPS
Description: Removes the 50 FPS cap for some game content, such as camera movement and dynamic lighting.

Name: VSync mode
Description: Controls whether the frame rate should be synchronized with your monitor's refresh rate. If set to 'off', the FPS target option will be used instead. If set to 'adaptive', FPS will be limited to your monitor's refresh rate, which saves power. If set to 'on', the game will attempt to match your monitor's refresh rate exactly , but if it can't keep up, FPS will be halved until it catches up . This option is rarely desired. Note: GPUs that don't support Adaptive VSync will silently fall back to 'on'.

Name: FPS target
Description: Controls the maximum number of frames per second. This setting only applies if Unlock FPS is enabled and VSync mode is set to 'off'.

Name: Color blindness
Description: Adjust colors to make them more distinguishable for people with a certain type of color blindness.

Name: Blindness intensity
Description: Specifies how intense the color blindness adjustment should be.

Name: Saturation
Description: Controls the saturation of the final rendered image. Intended to be kept between 0% and 120%.

Name: Contrast
Description: Controls the contrast of the final rendered image. Intended to be kept between 90% and 110%.

Name: Brightness
Description: Controls the brightness of the game, excluding the UI. Adjust until the circle on the left is barely visible.

Name: Shadow mode
Description: Render fully dynamic shadows. 'Off' completely disables shadows. 'Fast' enables fast shadows without any texture detail. 'Detailed' enables shadows with support for texture detail.

Name: Shadow quality
Description: The resolution of the shadow map. Higher resolutions result in higher quality shadows, at the cost of higher GPU usage.

Name: Shadow filtering
Description: Filtering technique used when smoothing the edges of shadows. 'Smooth low' smooths the shadow pixels evenly (PCF 2x2). 'Smooth high' smooths the shadow pixels evenly (PCF 3x3). 'Dithered low' smooths out pixelation using dithering. 'Dithered high' smooths out pixelation using dithering (PCF 2x2). 'Pixelated' retains slightly pixelated shadow edges. 'Soft shadows' produces realistically soft shadows, at the cost of performance.

Name: Shadow transparency
Description: Enable partial support for taking model transparency into account.

Name: Roof shadows
Description: Always cast shadows from roofs, even when they are hidden.

Name: Terrain shadows
Description: Allow terrain to cast shadows. May cause visual artifacts on slopes.

Name: Remove shadow pop-in
Description: Render a potentially much larger part of the scene, to avoid shadows popping in and out based on what the camera currently sees. May significantly impact performance.

Name: Vanilla shadows
Description: Choose whether shadows built into models by Jagex should be hidden. This does not affect clickboxes. 'Show in PvM' will retain shadows for falling crystals during the Olm fight and other useful cases. 'Prefer in PvM' will do the above and also disable 117 HD's dynamic shadows in such cases.

Name: Lights
Description: The maximum number of dynamic lights visible at once. Reducing this may improve performance.

Name: Object lights
Description: Adds dynamic lights to objects, such as lamps and fires.

Name: NPC lights
Description: Adds dynamic lights to some NPCs, excluding pets and followers.

Name: Pet lights
Description: Adds dynamic lights to pets and followers.

Name: Animation lights
Description: Adds dynamic lights to spells and other graphical effects.

Name: Projectile lights
Description: Adds dynamic lights to some projectiles.

Name: Water sun & moon reflections
Description: Enables sun and moon highlights on water, including the fake sun when day & night is disabled.

Name: Underwater caustics
Description: Apply underwater lighting effects to imitate sunlight passing through waves on the surface.

Name: Cycle mode
Description: Controls the day & night cycle behavior. 'Off' disables the day & night cycle entirely. 'Default' shows everyone the same sky, with one complete day passing per hour. 'Real-time' follows your local time, roughly matching the real sun in your hemisphere. 'Custom' follows the sun and moon at the configured location, respecting the Custom cycle duration. 'Dawn' shows the sky just before sunrise. 'Sunrise' shows a constant sunrise. 'Day' shows constant daytime. 'Sunset' shows a constant sunset. 'Dusk' shows the sky just after sunset. 'Night' shows constant night-time.

Name: Night brightness
Description: Simulates your eyes adapting to darkness by brightening night-time lighting. '0%' disables night brightness adaptation entirely. '100%' yields good visibility at night. Values above 100% amplify the adjustment further, if needed.

Name: Stars
Description: 'Off' hides stars. 'Realistic' follows the sky's celestial rotation. 'Artistic' rotates horizontally with slight parallax. 'Static' keeps the realistic star field fixed in place.

Name: Nebulae
Description: Show clouds of cosmic dust and gas in the night sky.

Name: Moon behavior
Description: Controls how the moon moves across the sky. 'Disabled' hides the moon, keeping half-moon illumination for scene lighting. 'Realistic orbit' makes the moon orbit naturally, independent of the sun. 'Mirror the sun' keeps the moon opposite the sun. 'Static' keeps the moon at a fixed point in the sky.

Name: Moon phase
Description: Controls the portion of the moon which is lit by the sun. 'Dynamic' lights up the moon based on its position relative to the sun. All other options lock the moon in a particular lunar phase.

Name: Replace vanilla skyboxes
Description: Replace the game's built-in skybox models with 117 HD's own implementation.

Name: Custom cycle duration
Description: Configures how long each Custom day & night cycle lasts.

Name: Real-time latitude
Description: Advanced setting : Change the latitude coordinate for realistic sun and moon movement for a location on Earth. Only applies to Real-time and Custom cycle modes. Defaults to New York City. For southern latitudes, use negative values. For more precise timing, you can provide coordinates including decimals in the in-game chat with: ::117hd latlon <latitude> <longitude> To return to using the values specified in the config panel, type: ::117hd latlon reset

Name: Real-time longitude
Description: Advanced setting : Change the longitude coordinate for realistic sun and moon movement for a location on Earth. Only applies to Real-time and Custom cycle modes. Defaults to New York City. For western longitudes, use negative values. For more precise timing, you can provide coordinates including decimals in the in-game chat with: ::117hd latlon <latitude> <longitude> To return to using the values specified in the config panel, type: ::117hd latlon reset

Name: Seasonal theme
Description: Festive themes for Gielinor.

Name: Seasonal hemisphere
Description: Determines which hemisphere the 'Automatic' seasonal theme should consider.

Name: Seasonal foliage
Description: Allow seasonal themes to change the color of tree leaves.

Name: Fog depth mode
Description: Determines how the fog amount is controlled. 'Dynamic' changes fog depth based on the area, while 'Static' respects the manually defined fog depth.

Name: Static fog depth
Description: Specify how far from the edge fog should reach. This applies only when 'Fog depth mode' is set to 'Static'.

Name: Ground fog
Description: Enables a height-based fog effect that covers the ground in certain areas.

Name: Default sky
Description: Specify a sky color to use when the current area doesn't have a sky color defined. This only applies when the default summer seasonal theme is active. If set to 'RuneLite Skybox', the sky color from RuneLite's Skybox plugin will be used. If set to 'Old School Black', the sky will be black and water will remain blue, but for any other option, the water color will be influenced by the sky color.

Name: Override sky color
Description: Forces the default sky color to be used in all environments.

Name: Model textures
Description: Adds new textures to most models. If disabled, the standard game textures will be used instead.

Name: Ground textures
Description: Adds new textures to most ground tiles.

Name: Texture resolution
Description: Controls the resolution used for all in-game textures.

Name: Ground blending
Description: Controls whether ground tiles should blend into each other, or have distinct edges. When set to 'Textures only', textures may blend between tiles, but not their colors.

Name: Wind displacement
Description: Controls whether things like grass and leaves should be affected by wind.

Name: Character displacement
Description: Let players & NPCs affect things like grass whilst walking around.

Name: Hide vanilla water ripples
Description: Hide vanilla ripples found around objects floating in the water.

Name: Player-owned house themes
Description: Change the environmental lighting based on the POH style.

Name: CPU usage
Description: Specify how much of your processor the plugin should be allowed to use. If you play with multiple clients or use other heavy programs on the side, reducing this may improve their performance. Defaults to Max, allowing the processor to be fully utilized.

Name: Reduce CPU when unfocused
Description: Automatically reduce CPU load when the game has not been in focus for 15 seconds.

Name: Infernal cape
Description: Replace the infernal cape texture with a more detailed version. Note: with Anisotropic filtering above zero, the cape may look blurry when zoomed out.

Name: Vanilla color banding
Description: Blend between colors similarly to how it works in vanilla, with clearly defined bands of color. This isn't really noticeable on textured surfaces, and is intended to be used without ground textures.

Name: Low memory mode
Description: Turns off features which require extra memory, such as model caching, faster scene loading & extended scene loading.

Name: Color filter
Description: Apply a color filter to the game as a post-processing effect.

Name: Remove vertex snapping
Description: Removes vertex snapping from most animations. Most animations are barely affected by this, and it only has an effect if the animation smoothing plugin is turned off. To see quite clearly what impact this option has, a good example is the godsword idle animation.

Name: Fill gaps in terrain
Description: Attempt to patch all holes in the ground, such as around trapdoors and ladders.

Name: Flat shading
Description: Gives a more low-poly look to the game.

Name: Glare intensity
Description: Reduce the glow around the sun & moon and their bright water reflections.

Name: Zone streaming
Description: Load zones in parallel in the background, switching to new scenes almost instantly. You will see zones appear when they are loaded, instead of having to wait for them all at once.

Name: Wireframe
Description: Show the edges of individual triangles in the scene.

Name: Use legacy renderer
Description: The new renderer is required for sailing content, and generally performs better than the legacy renderer.

Name: Use legacy brightness
Description: Whether the legacy brightness option below should be applied. We recommend leaving this disabled.

Name: Legacy brightness
Description: Controls the strength of the sun and ambient lighting. A brightness value of 20 is the default.

Name: Legacy shadow distance
Description: The maximum draw distance for shadows. Shorter distances result in higher quality shadows.

Name: Legacy model batching
Description: With the legacy renderer, model batching improves performance by reusing identical models within the same frame. May cause instability and graphical bugs, particularly if Jagex makes engine changes.

Name: Legacy model caching
Description: With the legacy renderer, model caching improves performance by saving and reusing model data from previous frames. May cause instability or graphical bugs, particularly if Jagex makes engine changes.

Name: Legacy cache size
Description: Size of the model cache in mebibytes (slightly more than megabytes). Generally, 512 MiB is plenty, with diminishing returns the higher you go. Minimum=64 MiB, maximum=16384 MiB

Name: Legacy gray colors
Description: Previously, HD attempted to reduce overexposure by capping the maximum color brightness, which changed white colors into dull shades of gray. This option brings back that old behavior.

Name: Legacy Theatre of Blood
Description: Previously, Theatre of Blood used to look a whole lot more blue, which some people grew really used to. This option brings back that same old look.

Name: Legacy TzHaar city reskin
Description: Recolors the TzHaar city of Mor Ul Rek to give it an appearance similar to that of its 2008 HD variant.

Name: Legacy boat silhouettes
Description: Renders boat silhouettes with textures like before.

Name: Disable environmental lighting
Description: Disable lighting tuned per environment, falling back to bright sunlight everywhere.

Name: Legacy lightning
Description: Crudely simulates lightning in areas such as Barrows and deep Wilderness.

Name: Preserve vanilla normals
Description: Originally, 117 HD would respect vanilla normals, but these are often less accurate.

Name: Shading mode
Description: If you prefer playing without shadows, maybe you'll prefer vanilla shading or no shading as well. Keep in mind, with vanilla shading used alongside shadows, you can end up with double shading.

Name: Decouple water from sky color
Description: Some people prefer the water staying blue even with a different sky color active.

Name: Simple boat silhouettes
Description: Skip rendering animated objects when boats are flattened beneath other boats.

Name: Night adaptation everywhere
Description: Apply Day & night's 'Night brightness' adaptation to all dark scenes.

Name: Tiled lighting
Description: Allows rendering a lot more lights simultaneously. Disabled by default on older Intel GPUs.

Name: Image load store
Description: If you experience any issues with tiled lighting, disabling this might help.

Name: Indirect draw
Description: Indirect draw is currently only enabled automatically for Nvidia GPUs. Enabling this might improve performance, if it is supported by your system.

Name: Storage buffers
Description: Storage buffers may improve performance, but may also cause graphical artifacts on some hardware. By default, we disable this automatically for Intel GPUs, since older ones can be problematic.

Name: Point sprites
Description: Controls whether GL_POINT_SPRITE should be used. The fallback uses instanced triangles.

Name: Multithreaded model processing
Description: Process multiple models in parallel to improve performance for animated models.

Name: Windows HDR correction
Description: Correctly simulates SDR gamma 2.2 when Windows is in HDR mode. Note: this does not enable HDR. It only works around an issue within Windows' HDR implementation.

Name: Intel-based Mac workaround
Description: Workaround for visual artifacts found on some Intel GPU drivers on macOS.

Name: Centroid qualifier
Description: Prevents artifacts when MSAA is enabled.
